301-program-requirements: Combine with another Arts discipline, seeing an adviser in each. Keep program GPA and CGPA at 3.00.
301-jewish-language: 0–6 credits, reaching advanced level in one Jewish language. If competent, you may substitute other courses.
301-areas-of-jewish-studies: 15–21 credits planned with an adviser, reaching advanced level in one area.
304-about-languages-literatures-and-cult: European and Latin American cultures in a global context: European Literature and Culture, German, Hispanic, Italian, Latin American and Caribbean, Liberal Arts, and Russian and Slavic. Also film, eco-criticism, literary theory, book history and digital humanities.

Builds skills in at least one language, for business, government, media and cultural careers. Graduate programs in German, Hispanic, Italian and Russian. For grad school, take honours or joint honours; B.A. & Sc. students can't take honours.
You may need approval for language courses. Placement tests can be booked before term with the language adviser. You can start at a higher level with approved prior courses.
Undergraduate Director: Daniel W. Pratt. Graduate Director: Lyudmila Parts.
304-european-literature-and-culture: How European culture developed and connects, through literature and arts from the Middle Ages on. No second language needed. Adviser: Stephanie Posthumus.
304-german-studies: German literature with cross-disciplinary research, from the Enlightenment to migration and multiculturalism, strong in philosophy, critical theory, philology, cinema and media. Individual mentoring. B.A. & Sc. students can't take German honours. Adviser: Tove Holmes.
304-hispanic-studies: Literature, intellectual history and civilization of Spain and Latin America, and Spanish. Exchanges with Salamanca, UNAM, Universidad de las Américas Puebla and others.
Adviser: Jose Jouve-Martin. AP credits and courses at other Québec universities don't count toward the Minor.
305-italian-studies: Classics and contemporary Italian culture, rigorous language training, literature in Italian and English, and film, with visiting scholars on politics, immigration and social change. Adviser: Eugenio Bolongaro.
305-latin-american-and-caribbean-studies: Honours: comprehensive interdisciplinary base for graduate or professional school, with a B+ (3.30) program average on top of CGPA 3.0.
Joint Honours: program GPA 3.30, CGPA 3.00, at least 9 of 36 credits at 400+, with an adviser in each department. Neither is open to B.A. & Sc. students. Adviser: Yann le Polain de Waroux.
305-liberal-arts: A personalized major with a foreign language, in one of three streams: literature and the arts; history, culture and society; or philosophy and religion. Distribution rules cover levels, disciplines, regions and periods. It requires a language minor other than English or French, depending on your background.
Honours adds courses and independent research with a professor of your choice, with program GPA 3.30 and overall 3.00. Not open to B.A. & Sc. students. Adviser: Matteo Soranzo.
305-russian-and-slavic-studies: Québec's only full undergraduate and graduate program, and among North America's largest, with about 100 major or minor students a year. Useful for government, nonprofits, comparative literature and linguistics. Adviser: Daniel W. Pratt.
306-program-description: How European culture developed and connects, through literature and arts from the Middle Ages to now. No second language needed.
306-complementary-courses-15-credits: 9–15 from the list, at least 6 at 300+. With advanced language, GERM, HISP, ITAL and RUSS courses in those languages count. At most 6 per area, not counting LLCU 210. 0–6 from CLAS, ENGL and FREN literature.
307-program-description: Proficiency in German plus an introduction to the culture, expandable to the German Studies Major. You can start higher with prior courses. Beginners' and Intermediate run as intensive one-term or spanned two-term courses.
307-complementary-courses-18-credits: Language courses, or any course above 325 taught in German.
308-program-description: German culture from the 18th century on, through literature, philosophy, film, theory and art, complementing other studies. Expandable to a Major.
308-complementary-courses-18-credits: Taught in English or German. At most 6 LLCU with approval. No Beginners' or Intermediate language; GERM 325 counts.
309-program-description: A rigorous look at German cultural life since the 18th century, with German as a core part and most courses taught in it, teaching you to read and interpret complex works and their significance.
310-program-description: The same, with all courses in German. Departmental approval; you can start in first year. Program GPA 3.30, CGPA 3.00, plus a minor in another unit.
310-complementary-courses-54-credits: 6 credits pre-20th century, at most 6 LLCU and 9 GERM in English with approval, 3 at 400.
311-program-description: The same core, normally in German, with another discipline. See an adviser in each department. Departmental approval, program GPA 3.30, CGPA 3.00.
311-complementary-courses-33-credits: German language stream (mostly in German) or translation stream (German or English). 6 credits pre-20th century. In the language stream, at most 9 LLCU or English-taught with approval, and 3 at 400.
312-program-description: A foundation in Spanish language and culture, expandable to the Major.
312-complementary-courses-18-credits: 0–12 of language; 6–18 of other Hispanic Studies, at most 6 in English. AP credits don't count.
312-program-description-2: Literature, intellectual history and civilization of Spain and Latin America, and Spanish, broadening communication and critical reasoning. Exchanges with Salamanca, UNAM, Puebla and others.
313-hispanic-literature-and-culture: 6–30 credits, at least 6 at 400+. At most 12 in English.
313-program-description: In-depth language and culture of Spain and Latin America: literature, film, digital humanities and intellectual history. Needs a first-year Spanish course with B+, program GPA 3.30, CGPA 3.00, and an 18-credit minor elsewhere.
313-complementary-courses-42-credits: At least 9 at 400+; the rest in Spanish at intermediate level or above. At most 18 in English.
313-program-description-2: Literature and culture of the Spanish-speaking world, with exchanges available, combined with another Arts discipline. See an adviser in each. Program GPA 3.30, CGPA 3.00.
314-complementary-courses-30-credits: 6–12 introductory; 18–24 at 300+, with 9 at 400+ (not HISP 490D). At most 12 in English.
314-complementary-courses-18-credits: 12–18 from Groups A and B combined; 0–6 from Group C, taught in English.
314-group-b-courses-taught-in-italian: Only one of ITAL 250 or ITAL 255 counts.
315-program-description: Meet a departmental adviser before registering.
315-complementary-courses-36-credits: Group A language, 0–12: no knowledge means 12; some knowledge means 6 from ITAL 210D, 215D or 216; competency can substitute from B and C. Consult the Department on placement.
Group B in Italian, at least 12, at most 6 at 200. Group C in English, 0–12.
316-program-description: Departmental approval, so consult early; qualified students may start in first year. Program GPA 3.30, CGPA 3.00.
316-required-courses-6-credits: One of the two honours thesis courses.
316-complementary-courses-48-credits: 9 at 400+. Group A 0–12, Group B 30–48, Groups C and D 0–9 combined. With advanced standing, replace language with B, C and D.
317-program-description: Combine with another Arts discipline, with an adviser in each. Departmental approval; may start in first year. Program GPA 3.30, CGPA 3.00.
317-complementary-courses-30-credits: 6 at 400+. Group A 0–12, Group B 12–30, Groups C and D 0–18 combined. With advanced standing, replace language.
318-program-description: A broad interdisciplinary view of the region, expandable to the Major.
318-complementary-courses-15-credits: 3–6 from each of two lists. 3–9 chosen with the Adviser, across two disciplines if more than one, at least one at 300+. At most 6 of Spanish or Portuguese.
318-english: Counts when the topic relates to the region.
319-geography: GEOG 404 counts only when the topic relates to Panama.
319-required-courses-18-credits: Intermediate Spanish (HISP 219 or 220D, or equivalent) is needed for HISP 243 and 244.
319-complementary-courses-21-credits: With the Adviser, from at least two disciplines, at least 6 at 300+, at most 6 of Spanish or Portuguese language.
